title: Q and U Best Friends
kidRule: In English words, Q almost never goes anywhere without its best friend U! Together Q-U usually says /kw/, as in QUESTION.
hint: We hear '/kw/'. One letter starts that sound, and its best friend always tags along right behind it. Which two letters are they?
reminder: The sound '/kw/' is spelled Q-U. Q always brings its best friend U.

check.question: Why is there a U right after the Q in QUESTION?
check.correctAnswer: Q almost always brings its best friend U along!
distractors: Because U always comes before the letter E
Because every asking word needs a U

words.def: Something you ask when you want to find out an answer.
words.sent: I asked a question about how rainbows are made.
words.story: In Spanish, a question gets two marks: an upside-down one at the start and a regular one at the end!
words.card: The wizard's *quest* began with one *question*: who took the last cookie?

words.def: One of four parts of something that are all the same size.
words.sent: I ate a quarter of the pizza all by myself.
words.story: The United States coin with this name has 119 tiny grooves around its edge!
words.card: I traded a *quarter* of my sandwich for a piece of dinosaur *art*!

words.sent: We were quiet so the baby could sleep.
words.story: An owl is so quiet when it flies that a mouse cannot hear it coming, thanks to its soft, fringed feathers!
words.card: My p*et* rock is very *quiet*, except when it snores!

words.def: A shape with four sides that are all the same length and four matching corners.
words.sent: I cut my sandwich into a perfect square.
words.story: A chessboard is made of 64 of these shapes, half of them light and half of them dark!
words.card: Help! We *are* stuck inside a *square* bubble!

words.def: Something that you ask for politely.
words.sent: The band played my song request at the party.
words.story: At many libraries you can make a request, and a book will travel from another library just for you!
words.card: My only *request* on this *quest* is a snack break!

words.def: Exactly the same in size, number, or amount.
words.sent: We each got an equal share of the pizza.
words.story: The = sign in math was invented in 1557 by a man who was tired of writing the same words over and over!
words.card: The ducks took *equal* turns to *qua*ck at the moon!

words.def: Something wet that you can pour, like water or juice.
words.sent: Water is a liquid that we drink every day.
words.story: Mercury is a shiny metal that is runny like water, even when it is not hot!
words.card: The *li*on spilled purple *liquid* all over the jungle floor!

words.def: To press something tightly from both sides.
words.sent: Please squeeze the orange to make some juice.
words.story: An octopus has no bones, so it can squeeze through a hole not much bigger than its eye!
words.card: One big *squeeze* and the toothpaste flew off on a bre*eez*y adventure!

words.def: A small furry animal with a bushy tail that climbs trees and collects nuts.
words.sent: A squirrel buried an acorn in our yard.
words.story: These animals forget where they buried many of their nuts, and some of those nuts grow into new trees!
words.card: The *squirrel* rode a bar*rel* of acorns down the hill!

words.def: A glass tank of water where fish live, or a building where you can visit sea animals.
words.sent: We watched the jellyfish glow at the aquarium.
words.story: A few aquariums are so big that whale sharks, the largest fish in the world, can swim around inside them!
words.card: The goldfish painted its *aquarium* bright *aqua* blue with its tail!
